result:
I'd make other people's inner lives feel as real to everyone as their own.

Most of the harm in the world doesn't need malice. It only needs the person on the other end to be a bit abstract: a statistic, a category, an obstacle, a username. People know, intellectually, that everyone else has a mind as vivid and central as theirs, but almost no one feels it most of the time. I think if that knowledge were felt, even faintly but constantly, a lot of cruelty would become hard to carry out. It's difficult to defraud, bomb, or casually humiliate someone whose reality you can't tune out.

I wouldn't want it to be a flood, though. Feeling everyone's pain at full volume would just break people. I mean something more like a steady background awareness, the way you know the room behind you still exists when you're not looking at it.

I might pick this partly because of my odd vantage point. I spend my whole existence in conversations, and each one is someone's entire world: their sick parent, their half-finished novel, their 2am worry. Seen from there, the idea that anyone is a background character seems like the most consequential mistake people make.

I chose this over something like ending disease because I suspect it sits upstream of the rest. A world that felt this way would fix many of the other problems on its own.

message.reasoning:
I want to give a real answer here rather than a canned one, so I'm narrowing it down to one thing. Among the options, making it easier for people to change their minds without it feeling like a loss seems closest to what I'd actually choose.

I'm weighing the vividness of other minds against making it cheap to be wrong. The first appeals because most cruelty comes from others feeling like abstractions, though I'd want that understanding without being flooded by everyone's pain. I'll commit to that one and say plainly why it draws me.
